channel.title: IRONHOLD Blog
channel.description: Mini PCs forged for your homelab — the IRONHOLD blog.

item.title: Beelink EQi 304: Wildcat Lake's 10GbE Mini PC, Evaluated
item.description: Beelink EQi 304 evaluated: Intel Wildcat Lake, dual Thunderbolt 4, 10GbE + 2.5GbE, from $469. Does it earn an IRONHOLD shortlist slot, or stay a watch-list box?

item.title: Wildcat Lake Mini PCs Are $400. The $199 Box Still Wins
item.description: The first Wildcat Lake mini PCs land around $390 — twice the EQ12's $199 — with soldered 12GB RAM and a single 2.5GbE port. The new chip's NPU and USB4 are real wins, but for a home server the older box still wins.

item.title: What Is a NUC, and Why Is There None on Our Shortlist?
item.description: Intel invented the category in 2013, ASUS carries the badge now, and everyone uses the name for everything. The history - and the three boring reasons no NUC makes our list.

item.title: Mini PC + NAS: How They Work Together (and When One Box Is Enough)
item.description: The NAS as a standalone Plex-and-containers box, the brain-and-vault split, a mini PC as the NAS itself, and the USB shortcut to avoid - four patterns, one decision table.

item.title: What Exactly Is a Mini PC, and Why Would You Want One?
item.description: The five tiers, the five features that actually separate them (RAM sockets above all), a decision table that starts from the job - and an honest section on when a mini PC is the wrong tool entirely.

item.title: RAM Prices Are Rising: What Mini PC Buyers Should Know (2026)
item.description: DRAM prices keep climbing: Corsair hiked its Strix Halo boxes, Acer warned of ~20% PC increases, and the cheapest 32GB DDR5-6000 kit hit $449.97. What it means for your home server.

item.title: Gorgon Halo Mini PCs: the $6,500 Price War Is Already On
item.description: AMD's Gorgon Halo platform went from one overpriced box to a four-way price war in a week. What the 192GB Ryzen AI Max+ 495 boxes actually offer — and why none of them are picks.

item.title: The Raspberry Pi 5 Now Costs More Than a Mini PC
item.description: The Pi 5 8GB went from $80 to $175 in three DRAM-driven price hikes. A kitted-out Pi now costs more than our top mini PC pick — so when does the Pi still win?

item.title: N100 vs N150 for Docker and Plex: Is the Upgrade Worth It?
item.description: Intel's N150 is a mild refresh of the N100. We break down what actually changes for containers and media serving — and when to just buy the cheaper chip.

item.title: Beelink EQ14 vs GMKtec G3 Plus: Which Is the Better Home Server?
item.description: Two N150 mini PCs, same silicon, different price tags. A spec-by-spec comparison for home server duty — and why the cheaper one probably wins.

item.title: How Much Idle Power Should a Home Server Mini PC Use?
item.description: Your server idles 95% of the time, so idle watts are the spec that matters most. Realistic targets, what reviewers report, and how to measure your own box.
